English: Sheepfold
Strongly fenced enclosures for sheep, with watch posts and shared grazing management. Local trade increases as wool becomes available.
Yurt Cluster
A growing assembly of yurts for herders and their families, with basic corrals and communal firepits improving organization and efficiency.
Pasture Camp
A crude encampment of tents and makeshift fences for livestock, marking the first efforts to settle and graze herds on the open steppe.
Steppe Corral
A fortified corral with timber fencing and semi-permanent shelters, allowing for larger herds and increased urban trade in livestock products.
Horse Herd
A sprawling network of fenced pastures for horses, with dedicated handlers and trade facilities. The city profits from breeding, trading, and improved defense.
Cattle Pen
Large, well-guarded pens for cattle, incorporating stone foundations and overseer lodges. The prosperity attracts merchants and provides a strong base for urban defense.
Wool Pavilion
A thriving market and craft hall for wool production, with covered trading pavilions and artisan guilds, drawing traders from afar.
Steppe Grazing
Vast, managed grazing lands with irrigation ditches and guard towers, maximizing herd size and ensuring the security of the citys food supply and trade.
Herdmasters Lodge
The residence and office of the chief herdmaster, with administrative staff, scribes, and a granary. Urban order and trade are at their zenith.
Nomad Enclosure
A grand complex of fortified livestock enclosures, markets, and administration, symbolizing the citys mastery of steppe herding and its economic might.
